steps.message:
# The hook collision line does not show what the hook will do

### What happens
`recording.mp4` (1:02) shows the client's *Hook Collisions* settings page, which shows how the
player's own hook collision line is configured, what each line colour means, and a preview of how the
line should look, together with a player using the grappling hook on a practice level. At several
moments the line contradicts the settings page or what the hook does right after it is fired: in its
colour, in where it ends, in how it is drawn, or by not being drawn at all. These are separate, independent defects, each affecting a different situation; fixing
one does not fix the others.

### Expected
While the setting is on, the line is always drawn from the player along the current aim, and it never
contradicts the settings page or what the hook does when it is fired along that aim. This must hold
everywhere, not only in the situations shown in the video.

### Environment
All.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

Inspect the attached video before making changes. You can pull individual frames out of it with
`ffmpeg` (installed in the image); some of the relevant moments last only a few frames. The video
describes observable behavior; it does not prescribe source files, internal names, or an
implementation strategy.

steps.message:
I fixed six separate problems with the hook collision line in `src/game/client/components/players.cpp` and `src/game/client/gameclient.cpp`. The client builds, but I haven't run the game or watched the line in play.

**I couldn't watch the video.** `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty and there's no `recording.mp4` anywhere on the system. Instead, I compared the line-drawing code against the code that actually moves the hook (`src/game/gamecore.cpp`) and against the settings page preview. So I can't be sure these are exactly the moments shown in the video.

**Not drawn at all**
- **Fractional hook settings:** hook speed and length were rounded down to whole numbers. If a level set the hook speed below 1, it became 0 and the line was skipped completely. They now keep their real values.

**Wrong colour**
- **Tees behind a wall:** a tee just behind a wall turned the line yellow (the "a tee" colour), even though the hook stops at the wall. Tees are now only checked up to where the hook hits the map.
- **Tees counted only when very close:** the line counted a tee as hit only within half the distance the real hook uses, so it could miss tees the hook would grab. It now uses the same distance as the hook.
- **Ground at the very end of the hook's reach:** the hook doesn't grab anything when it reaches full length in the same step it touches the ground, but the line still showed the "something hookable" colour. It now shows "nothing hookable".
- **Player hooking turned off:** if a server turns off hooking players, the line no longer shows the tee colour. It also now ignores leftover data for players who aren't currently in play.

**Wrong end point after a teleporter**
- **After a teleporter:** the line restarted exactly at the exit and measured the remaining hook length from there. The real hook starts slightly ahead of the exit and measures from that point, so the line ended in the wrong place. It now does the same as the hook.
- **Teleporters that send the hook into each other:** this could make the line calculation loop forever. It now stops after 16 teleports.

**Wrong shape**
- **Thick lines at an angle:** when the line width setting is above 0, its thickness was applied in the wrong direction. Any line that wasn't horizontal or vertical came out skewed or thin. It now has the same thickness as the settings preview at every angle.

I checked the settings page preview and found nothing wrong there. Nothing is committed.
